cohort: 24 women with severe percreta (Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics grades 3b and 3c) who underwent elective primary cesarean hysterectomy at a large UK tertiary referral center between 2011 and 2020
finding: The Soleymani-Alazzam-Collins technique for radical peripartum hysterectomy resulted in significantly less blood loss, more transverse incisions, and fewer intensive care unit admissions, without increasing surgical time, compared to standard care in women with severe placenta accreta spectrum.
mod_finding: The Soleymani-Alazzam-Collins technique for radical cesarean hysterectomy in cases of severe placenta accreta spectrum resulted in significantly more transverse incisions compared to standard care.
